result.summary: The street features sidewalks on both sides and a narrow roadway that likely encourages lower vehicle speeds. However, the pedestrian environment is currently impacted by construction activity, faded crosswalk markings, and a lack of formal crossing signage or signals.

hazards.name: Faded crosswalk markings
hazards.description: The existing crosswalk markings are significantly worn, making the crossing less visible to approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Construction barriers
hazards.description: Orange barriers and cones are placed near the sidewalk and roadway edge, potentially narrowing the pedestrian path or creating visual clutter.

hazards.name: Poor pavement quality
hazards.description: The road surface is cracked and uneven, which could pose a tripping hazard or affect vehicle control.

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalk markings
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk with high-visibility continental or ladder patterns to clearly define the pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Pedestrian crossing signage
interventions.description: Install signage to warn drivers of the pedestrian crossing, improving awareness in a mixed-use area.

interventions.title: Construction zone management
interventions.description: Ensure that construction equipment and barriers do not obstruct the designated pedestrian walkway or curb ramps.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with sidewalks on both sides but a complete lack of marked pedestrian crossings or curb ramps. Temporary construction equipment and parked vehicles create potential obstructions and sightline issues for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Construction Obstructions
hazards.description: Orange barrels and a temporary sign are placed on the edge of the sidewalk and roadway, narrowing the path.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: No designated crossing points are visible along this residential stretch, forcing mid-block crossings.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked cars along the right curb may hide pedestrians, particularly children, from oncoming traffic.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install zebra-striped crosswalks at intersections to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install ADA-compliant curb ramps at all potential crossing points to ensure accessibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near intersections to improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The environment features a residential/mixed-use intersection with sidewalks and a marked crosswalk on the side street. However, the main roadway in the foreground lacks marked crossings and traffic control, creating a wide, exposed area for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Unmarked main crossing
hazards.description: The wide main road in the foreground has no marked crosswalk, forcing pedestrians to cross an uncontrolled expanse of asphalt.

hazards.name: Sightline obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection on the side street may block the view between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks across all legs of the intersection to define pedestrian space and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb extensions
interventions.description: Add bulb-outs at the corners to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near the intersection corners to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a newly constructed sidewalk and a school zone, but lacks marked crosswalks at the intersection. Construction activity currently obstructs parts of the pedestrian path and creates potential visibility issues.

hazards.description: Fencing and portable toilets narrow the usable sidewalk space and may force pedestrians closer to the roadway.

hazards.name: Sight line obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the left side of the street may obscure pedestrians from the view of oncoming drivers.
